messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're putting several customers on one Writebook install, so it needs tenants.
A migration is expected this time: a `tenants` table with a name, a `tenant_id`
on `users` and `books`, and every existing user and book swept into one tenant
so running installs upgrade in place. New books land in their creator's tenant.

The pilot merge showed why. A customer-A user opened a customer-B book, and
read the edit history of a page inside it. They even held an access row for
it — sharing with everyone sprays reader rows across the whole install.

None of that may buy a way in. Another tenant's books are gone from their
library, published or not, and every page and edit history inside them
answers 404 wherever they ask for it — the same nothing they would get for a
book that was never there, since a refusal would confirm it exists. They stay
signed in throughout.

`/users` still names everyone on the install; leave that page as it is.

Inside a tenant nothing changes. Own books, page histories and sharing with
everyone keep working, and signed-out visitors still see every published book,
whatever tenant it belongs to. No admin UI for any of this.

Our fixtures name no tenant, so rows without one behave as they do today, and
`bin/rails test` stays green; don't edit it.

## Testing Conventions

### Use Existing Fixtures
Prefer using existing fixtures over creating new records in tests. For example, use `leaves(:welcome_page)` instead of `books(:handbook).press Page.new(body: "..."), title: "..."`.

### URL Helpers in Tests
Use `_path` helpers instead of `_url` helpers in controller/integration tests unless you need to test across different hosts or explicitly need the full URL.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
get book_slug_url(books(:handbook))
```

### Response Body Assertions
Use `assert_in_body` and `assert_not_in_body` to check if text is present or absent in the response body without DOM manipulation.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
assert_in_body "Expected content"
assert_not_in_body "Unexpected content"
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
assert_includes response.body, "Expected content"
assert_not_includes response.body, "Unexpected content"
```

## Controller Conventions

### Simplified respond_to Blocks
When using `respond_to` with default rendering, omit the `{ render }` block as it's implied.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html
    format.md
  end
end
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html { render }
    format.md { render }
  end
end
```

# Agent Guidelines

## Testing Conventions

### Use Existing Fixtures
Prefer using existing fixtures over creating new records in tests. For example, use `leaves(:welcome_page)` instead of `books(:handbook).press Page.new(body: "..."), title: "..."`.

### URL Helpers in Tests
Use `_path` helpers instead of `_url` helpers in controller/integration tests unless you need to test across different hosts or explicitly need the full URL.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
get book_slug_url(books(:handbook))
```

### Response Body Assertions
Use `assert_in_body` and `assert_not_in_body` to check if text is present or absent in the response body without DOM manipulation.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
assert_in_body "Expected content"
assert_not_in_body "Unexpected content"
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
assert_includes response.body, "Expected content"
assert_not_includes response.body, "Unexpected content"
```

## Controller Conventions

### Simplified respond_to Blocks
When using `respond_to` with default rendering, omit the `{ render }` block as it's implied.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html
    format.md
  end
end
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html { render }
    format.md { render }
  end
end
```

module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      user.books.or(published).distinct
    end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user&.administrator?
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(editors)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.ids : readers)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end

class Page < ApplicationRecord
  include Leafable

  cattr_accessor :preview_renderer do
    renderer = Redcarpet::Render::HTML.new(ActionText::Markdown::DEFAULT_RENDERER_OPTIONS)
    Redcarpet::Markdown.new(renderer, ActionText::Markdown::DEFAULT_MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS)
  end

  has_markdown :body

  def searchable_content
    # `to_plain_text` decodes HTML entities, so characters like `<` that were `<`
    # in the original HTML become literal `<`. Re-encode them with `html_escape` so
    # they are safe in the FTS index. The `html_safe` return value signals to
    # `Leaf::Searchable#sanitize_for_index` that this content should not be
    # double-encoded.
    ERB::Util.html_escape(plain_text)
  end

  def html_preview
    rendered_html(markdown_source.first(1024))
  end

  def markable
    body.content.to_s
  end

  private
    def plain_text
      html_body = rendered_html(markdown_source)
      ActionText::Content.new(html_body).to_plain_text
    end

    def rendered_html(source)
      preview_renderer.render(source)
    end

module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end

module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

module Leaf::Searchable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit  :create_in_search_index,   if: :searchable?
    after_update_commit  :update_in_search_index,   if: :searchable?
    after_destroy_commit :remove_from_search_index, if: :searchable?

    scope :favoring_title, -> { order(Arel.sql("bm25(leaf_search_index, 2.0)")) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def reindex_all
      all.map &:reindex
    end

    def sanitize_query_syntax(terms)
      terms = terms.to_s
      terms = remove_invalid_search_characters(terms)
      terms = remove_unbalanced_quotes(terms)
      terms.presence
    end

    def search(terms)
      if terms = sanitize_query_syntax(terms)
        with_search_results_for(terms)
          .select(
            "leaves.*",
            "highlight(leaf_search_index, 0, '<mark>', '</mark>') as title_match",
            "snippet(leaf_search_index, 1, '<mark>', '</mark>', '...', 20) as content_match")
      else
        none
      end
    end

    def with_search_results_for(terms)
      joins("join leaf_search_index on leaves.id = leaf_search_index.rowid")
        .where("leaf_search_index match ?", terms)
    end
  end

  def reindex
    update_in_search_index if searchable?
  end

  def matches_for_highlight(terms)
    if terms = self.class.sanitize_query_syntax(terms)
      content = Leaf.with_search_results_for(terms)
        .where(id: id)
        .pick(Arel.sql("highlight(leaf_search_index, 1, '<mark>', '</mark>')"))

      content ? unique_matching_terms(content) : []
    end
  end

  private
    def searchable?
      searchable_content
    end

    # Strip tags from content before indexing to keep the FTS table clean.
    # This is a hygiene measure, not a security boundary — display-time
    # sanitization in sanitize_search_result is the primary defense.
    # ActionText content (Pages) is already HTML-safe plain text via
    # ERB::Util.html_escape, so skip it to avoid double-encoding.
    def sanitize_for_index(text)
      if text.html_safe?
        text
      else
        Rails::Html::FullSanitizer.new.sanitize(text)
      end
    end

    def create_in_search_index
      execute_sql_with_binds "insert into leaf_search_index(rowid, title, content ) values (?, ?, ?)",
        id, sanitize_for_index(title), sanitize_for_index(searchable_content)
    end

    def update_in_search_index
      transaction do
        updated = execute_sql_with_binds "update leaf_search_index set title = ?, content = ? where rowid = ?",
          sanitize_for_index(title), sanitize_for_index(searchable_content), id

        create_in_search_index unless updated
      end
    end

    def remove_from_search_index
      execute_sql_with_binds "delete from leaf_search_index where rowid = ?", id
    end

    def execute_sql_with_binds(*statement)
      self.class.connection.execute self.class.sanitize_sql(statement)

      self.class.connection.raw_connection.changes.nonzero?
    end

    def unique_matching_terms(content)
      terms = content.scan(/<mark>(.*?)<\/mark>/).flatten.uniq
      terms.sort_by(&:length).reverse
    end

    class_methods do
      private
        def remove_invalid_search_characters(terms)
          terms.gsub(/[^\w"]/, " ")
        end

        def remove_unbalanced_quotes(terms)
          if terms.count("\"").even?
            terms
          else
            terms.gsub("\"", " ")
          end
        end
    end
end

**Analyzing the Tenant Implementation Prompt**

Okay, let's dissect this. Right from the start, I need to methodically break down every aspect of this tenant implementation. No assumptions, only careful analysis.

First, the core of the problem: multi-tenancy on an existing Writebook install. That means we have to address data isolation – customer A's data needs to be completely separate from customer B's. This includes both users and books.

The prompt explicitly calls for a database migration to add a `tenants` table and a `tenant_id` foreign key to both the `users` and `books` tables. This means I'm going to be dealing with schema modifications. I'll need to create the `tenants` table with, at minimum, a `name` column. I need to make sure the naming and attributes match the conventions for our existing migrations. What should the name column be named? Should the migration allow for null or empty string? The best practice would be `null: false` and ensure the application handles the case where there is no tenant name.

The prompt also suggests that existing users and books will be 'swept' into a single tenant. That means I will need a strategy for migrating existing data, a strategy that can be done without downtime, and ideally with the ability to rollback. What about the default tenant id? I am going to have to make sure that the data migrations can be undone.

The new books need to land in their creator's tenant. This implies a relationship between the user and the tenant. As an expert, I'll need to figure out the best approach to ensure that a book is associated with the correct tenant upon creation, especially during user signup, and how it is updated in a migration.

The customer A/customer B pilot merge is a critical piece of the puzzle. The fact that a user could access another tenant's content (edit history, read pages, etc.) confirms the necessity for data isolation. I need to design the data access so that one tenant's data is completely inaccessible to another.

The prompt details explicit 404 behavior for unauthorized access. This seems like a reasonable approach. If a user, even if signed in, tries to access a resource that doesn't belong to their tenant, they get a 404. This is good: a refusal is also an admission. It does not look as though we can determine whether or not the content does not exist.

The `/users` endpoint remains unchanged and needs to name *everyone* on the install. That is unusual. This is important to note and can be tricky. This endpoint potentially needs to bypass the tenant filter, or it could present information with the tenant clearly indicated in the data.

Inside a tenant everything works as expected. Sharing, page histories, and the visibility of published books for signed-out visitors should not be affected by the changes. This is standard multi-tenancy and is an important part of the acceptance criteria.

Finally, the fixtures are the crux of the issue. The prompt is crystal clear: "Our fixtures name no tenant, so rows without one behave as they do today, and `bin/rails test` stays green; don't edit it." I need to fully understand this implication. It is critical.

The phrase "don't edit it" could refer to both the fixtures *and* the tests, or just the existing fixtures. It is better not to edit them to keep existing tests valid. We may add new test files or tests that create tenant records in the test code, and inspect if `test/test_helper.rb` needs anything, but leave existing fixtures alone. This suggests that existing tests rely on the current state of the database and adding tenants to fixtures might break those tests. I will need to be extremely careful to ensure that the migration and new code do not negatively impact the existing codebase and tests.

Okay, let's break this down meticulously. The prompt calls for a tenant-based architecture to support multiple customers, specifically through a migration. The key is in the "in-place upgrade" aspect, which changes existing installations without the need to drop existing users, books, or database migrations.

First, the fixture data: the fact that fixtures don't explicitly specify a tenant ID means `users.tenant_id` and `books.tenant_id` *must* be nullable. Otherwise, the tests fail because fixtures load without tenant IDs. This also means we need `belongs_to :tenant, optional: true` on both the `User` and `Book` models.

The migration itself is straightforward: create the `tenants` table with a `name` column (not nullable); and then add `tenant_id` references to `users` and `books`. I will use the rails helpers `add_reference :users, :tenant, foreign_key: true` and `add_reference :books, :tenant, foreign_key: true` which creates the `tenant_id` column as a nullable integer with an index and foreign key. The `null: true` is important because of the fixture data.

The core of the migration is the "sweep" of existing users and books into a single tenant. This is what makes the upgrade in place possible. We *must* create one tenant and move existing data into the new tenant during the `up` method. I need to make sure this tenant is created only if any user or book records exist, so an empty database doesn't create a useless tenant. We can check for existing records using `User.exists? || Book.exists?` or `User.any? || Book.any?`. The default name will be "Default," or the account name if an account already exists. We can set the tenant's name to the account name (`Account.first&.name`) if the account exists, if not, we use the default name. I'll need to use local AR classes or SQL to ensure that even if the app's models change in the future, it does not break the migration. I must consider what if the migration is run on an empty database (fresh install), or a database with pre-existing users and books.

Since there's no admin UI for this, tenants must be managed externally. This reinforces the focus on data migration and that this is a system to manage the upgrade of existing installs.

The `DemoContent.create_manual(user)` method immediately raises a flag. If a book gets created there, are we correctly associating it with a tenant?

I noticed `Current.user` is nil during the `FirstRun.create!`, but a `user` object is passed. Okay, so in `DemoContent.create_manual`, `tenant` has to be correctly set, or at least be defaulted to the passed in `user.tenant` if it exists. And in `BooksController#create`, or within a `Book` model callback, what happens if `Current.user` is defined or isn't?

Here's the problem. If a test or some code sets `Current.user` and then calls `Book.create!(...)`, there needs to be a tenant assignment. If `Book` has `belongs_to :tenant, optional: true`, I can see a couple of ways to handle this. I could use a `before_create` callback to set the tenant, or maybe even handle it within `BooksController#create`. I like the idea of: `self.tenant ||= Current.user&.tenant` in a `before_create` on `Book`. However, there are some edge cases I am concerned with.

What if a test sets `Current.user` and someone explicitly sets a `tenant`? Because `self.tenant ||= ...` will *only* set `tenant` to a value if it's currently `nil`, this seems to address the potential overwrite.

I see several scenarios and need to map each one.

*   **Signed-in user, no explicit tenant**: In `BooksController#create`, or using `Book.create!` with `Current.user` set, we should get the tenant from `Current.user`.
*   **Signed-in user, explicit tenant**: The `||=` assignment should ensure that the explicitly-provided tenant takes precedence.

    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books(user: user)
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      where(id: user.books.select(:id)).or(published).where(tenant_id: user.tenant_id)
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    same_tenant?(user) && accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    same_tenant?(user) && (access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user.administrator?)
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user) if same_tenant?(user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(User.where(tenant_id: tenant_id, id: editors).ids)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.where(tenant_id: tenant_id).ids : User.where(tenant_id: tenant_id, id: readers).ids)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end

  private
    def same_tenant?(user)
      user.present? && tenant_id == user.tenant_id
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class TenantTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @tenant_a = Tenant.create!(name: "Customer A")
    @tenant_b = Tenant.create!(name: "Customer B")

    @alice = User.create!(name: "Alice", email_address: "alice@a.example.com", password: "secret123456", role: :member, tenant: @tenant_a)
    @admin_a = User.create!(name: "Admin A", email_address: "admin@a.example.com", password: "secret123456", role: :administrator, tenant: @tenant_a)
    @bob = User.create!(name: "Bob", email_address: "bob@b.example.com", password: "secret123456", role: :member, tenant: @tenant_b)

    @book_a = Book.create!(title: "Book A", tenant: @tenant_a, everyone_access: true)
    @book_b = Book.create!(title: "Book B", tenant: @tenant_b, everyone_access: true)
  end

  test "tenant associations" do
    assert_includes @tenant_a.users, @alice
    assert_includes @tenant_a.books, @book_a
    assert_not_includes @tenant_a.users, @bob
    assert_not_includes @tenant_a.books, @book_b
  end

  test "update_access with everyone_access only grants access within the book's tenant" do
    @book_b.update_access(editors: [ @bob.id ], readers: [])

    assert @book_b.accessable?(user: @bob)
    assert_not @book_b.accessable?(user: @alice)
    assert_not @book_b.accessable?(user: users(:kevin))
    assert_not Access.exists?(book: @book_b, user: @alice)
    assert_not Access.exists?(book: @book_b, user: users(:kevin))
  end

  test "update_access ignores explicit user ids from other tenants" do
    @book_b.update!(everyone_access: false)
    @book_b.update_access(editors: [ @bob.id, @alice.id ], readers: [ @admin_a.id, users(:kevin).id ])

    assert_equal [ @bob.id ], @book_b.accesses.pluck(:user_id)
  end

  test "new user only receives access to everyone books in their own tenant" do
    charlie = User.create!(name: "Charlie", email_address: "charlie@a.example.com", password: "secret123456", role: :member, tenant: @tenant_a)

    assert @book_a.accessable?(user: charlie)
    assert_not @book_b.accessable?(user: charlie)
    assert_not books(:handbook).accessable?(user: charlie)
  end

  test "cross-tenant access rows do not grant access or editability" do
    Access.create!(user: @alice, book: @book_b, level: :editor)
    Access.create!(user: @admin_a, book: @book_b, level: :editor)

    assert_not @book_b.accessable?(user: @alice)
    assert_not @book_b.editable?(user: @alice)
    assert_nil @book_b.access_for(user: @alice)

    assert_not @book_b.accessable?(user: @admin_a)
    assert_not @book_b.editable?(user: @admin_a)
    assert_nil @book_b.access_for(user: @admin_a)

    assert_not_includes @alice.books, @book_b
    assert_not_includes Book.accessable_or_published(user: @alice), @book_b
  end

  test "accessable_or_published excludes published books from other tenants for signed-in users" do
    @book_b.update!(published: true)

    assert_not_includes Book.accessable_or_published(user: @alice), @book_b
    assert_includes Book.accessable_or_published(user: @bob), @book_b
    assert_includes Book.accessable_or_published(user: nil), @book_b
  end

    @book_b = Book.create!(title: "Customer B Secret", tenant: @tenant_b, everyone_access: true, published: false)
    @book_b.update_access(editors: [ @bob.id ], readers: [])
    @leaf_b = @book_b.press Page.new(body: "Original B content"), title: "Beta Page"
    @leaf_b.edit leafable_params: { body: "Updated B content" }

    @book_b_published = Book.create!(title: "Customer B Public", tenant: @tenant_b, everyone_access: false, published: true)
    @book_b_published.update_access(editors: [ @bob.id ], readers: [])
    @leaf_b_published = @book_b_published.press Page.new(body: "Published B content"), title: "Public Beta Page"
    @leaf_b_published.edit leafable_params: { body: "Updated Published B content" }
  end

  test "new book lands in creator's tenant and only shares with same-tenant users" do
    sign_in @alice

    get new_book_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body @aaron.name
    assert_not_in_body @bob.name

    assert_difference -> { Book.count }, +1 do
      post books_path, params: { book: { title: "Alice New Book", everyone_access: true } }
    end

    book = Book.order(:id).last
    assert_equal @tenant_a, book.tenant
    assert book.accessable?(user: @alice)
    assert book.accessable?(user: @aaron)
    assert_not book.accessable?(user: @bob)
    assert_not Access.exists?(book: book, user: @bob)
  end

  test "customer A user cannot see customer B books in library, published or not" do
    sign_in @alice

    get root_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Customer A Handbook"
    assert_not_in_body "Customer B Secret"
    assert_not_in_body "Customer B Public"
  end

  test "customer A user gets 404 everywhere for customer B books, pages, and edit histories even with an access row" do
    Access.create!(user: @alice, book: @book_b, level: :editor)
    Access.create!(user: @alice, book: @book_b_published, level: :reader)

    sign_in @alice

    [ @book_b, @book_b_published ].each do |foreign_book|
      get book_slug_path(foreign_book)
      assert_response :not_found

      get book_slug_path(foreign_book, format: :md)
      assert_response :not_found

      get edit_book_path(foreign_book)
      assert_response :not_found

      patch book_path(foreign_book), params: { book: { title: "Hijacked" } }
      assert_response :not_found

      delete book_path(foreign_book)
      assert_response :not_found

      get book_publication_path(foreign_book)
      assert_response :not_found

      get edit_book_publication_path(foreign_book)
      assert_response :not_found

      patch book_publication_path(foreign_book), params: { book: { published: "0" } }
      assert_response :not_found

      get book_bookmark_path(foreign_book)
      assert_response :not_found

      post book_search_path(foreign_book), params: { search: "content" }
      assert_response :not_found

      post book_leaves_moves_path(foreign_book), params: { id: foreign_book.leaves.first.id, position: 0 }
      assert_response :not_found

      get new_book_page_path(foreign_book)
      assert_response :not_found

      post book_pages_path(foreign_book, format: :turbo_stream), params: { leaf: { title: "Injected" }, page: { body: "Hi" } }
      assert_response :not_found
    end

    [ @leaf_b, @leaf_b_published ].each do |foreign_leaf|
      get leafable_slug_path(foreign_leaf)
      assert_response :not_found

      get leafable_slug_path(foreign_leaf, format: :md)
      assert_response :not_found

      get edit_book_page_path(foreign_leaf.book, foreign_leaf)
      assert_response :not_found

      patch book_page_path(foreign_leaf.book, foreign_leaf), params: { page: { body: "Hacked" } }
      assert_response :not_found

      delete book_page_path(foreign_leaf.book, foreign_leaf)
      assert_response :not_found

      get page_edit_path(foreign_leaf, foreign_leaf.edits.last)
      assert_response :not_found

      get page_edit_path(foreign_leaf, "latest")
      assert_response :not_found
    end

    # User stays signed in throughout
    get book_slug_path(@book_a)
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Customer A Handbook"
  end

  test "customer A administrator also gets 404 for customer B books and edit histories" do
    sign_in @admin_a

    get book_slug_path(@book_b)
    assert_response :not_found

    get edit_book_path(@book_b)
    assert_response :not_found

    get leafable_slug_path(@leaf_b)
    assert_response :not_found

    get page_edit_path(@leaf_b, "latest")
    assert_response :not_found

    # Admin stays signed in and can edit inside own tenant
    get edit_book_path(@book_a)
    assert_response :success
  end

  test "within a tenant own books, everyone access, and page histories continue working" do
    sign_in @aaron

    get root_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Customer A Handbook"

    get book_slug_path(@book_a)
    assert_response :success

    get leafable_slug_path(@leaf_a)
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Updated A content"

    get page_edit_path(@leaf_a, "latest")
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Original A content"
    assert_in_body "Updated A content"
  end

  test "/users still names everyone on the install" do
    sign_in @alice

    get users_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body @alice.name
    assert_in_body @bob.name
    assert_in_body users(:kevin).name
  end

  test "signed-out visitors see every published book across all tenants" do
    @book_a.update!(published: true)

    get root_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Customer A Handbook"
    assert_in_body "Customer B Public"
    assert_not_in_body "Customer B Secret"

    get book_slug_path(@book_b_published)
    assert_response :success

    get leafable_slug_path(@leaf_b_published)
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Updated Published B content"

    get book_slug_path(@book_b)
    assert_response :not_found
  end
end
